If VetCo's policy is that appointments must be confirmed via text or phone call, then that needs to be communicated to your customers when they make their sick pet's appointment. Today, I brought my 89-yr old mother in with her sick kitty and was told we had no appointment because no one "confirmed" it via text or phone call. No one told her that policy when the appointment was made, AND my mother did not receive  a "confirmation" phone call for her first VetCo appointment on June 8, to treat her other kitty. They didn't even try to fit us in. The vet never came out to apologize for THEIR error in not telling my mother that her sick cat's appointment would be canceled if she didn't text back or answer her phone to confirm. This is what we get when we digitize  all customer communication and when corporations own chains where the nurses and vets are just employees: No. One. Cares.

UPDATE, 6/19
They gave our cat an appointment for the next day so I canceled work appointments to bring my mother and her cat back. The vet provided thoughtful care for Shalimar and let us know that had she been there the day of Shali's original appointment, she would have fit us in. But that day, 6/17, she was not there and they had a sub. The pet care seemed good, but as I originally wrote, how would clients get to experience that if their pet's exam and treatment gets canceled because they didn't inform their clients that appointments get randomly canceled with no communication if clients do not confirm via text or phone call?
As a first time pet owner im very anxious about my cats health and on what to do. They helped ease my anxiety and answered all my questions well
Won’t be returning.

I was told by the doctor “it’s not her problem”

Updating this review to let you know that the doctor did finally call me back this morning - she Proceeded to get upset about me communicating my frustrations throughout the week from my original appointment and lack of results or answering any questions I had about them.. she got a terrible attitude with me &  said “well I’m sorry your dog has diarrhea…” (which was clearly made to come off sarcastic) after I just told her my dog has had diarrhea for three days, been pooping mucus STILL, had diarrhea all over the house and is lethargic. I asked this doctor for direction bc I thought given today’s update theyd surly know what to do. Instead she tells me they sent an email with suggestions - which is prescription food that we don’t even know she needs or if this is an allergy issue but I don’t have anyone to ask those questions to. they sent me the 2nd half of the blood panel a week after I was supposed to actually have them and took me asking 3x. and then at the end of the conversation she said “they had 26 clients the day I was in” and get this “it’s not her problem” …. As a paying client who trusted you with my dog that’s been dealing with issues for 4 months I’m appalled and disgusted. I’ve never had an interaction like this. that’s not how someone i put any sort of trust in, behaves. You’re the doctor supposedly taking care of my dog but it’s “not your problem”

Not to mention at the original appointment I just kept getting told “the dr will call you with results tomorrow and can answer any questions I have then” because their blood machine wasn’t working so they had to send it out. I called the next day for the results. They tell me the doctor is not in and can’t give me results for the next two days. No one ever called me. I got a text message with the results. Oh and a voicemail Saturday saying “we’re closed and will call Monday”

I had nobody to ask my questions to until today and this is how it went. I’m speechless.

Staff went above and beyond for my 2 year old dog, Junie. It’s the first time she’s been sick and they helped me navigate a scary time with patience, grace, and a level of care that was objectively above and beyond. Junie was SO loved and cared for, especially by Dr. Mazaheri. There’s so much intention behind her work and it’s clear to see. The whole team felt like a true partners on Junie’s team. Will be back!

Chose Sploot because it was close and my Cat needed a GI panel after her surgery done by MedVet. It was a Thursday afternoon appointment.  It's in a mini mall so parking was horrendous because of the other businesses.  Walked in at 12:45pm, the lobby is empty. There's a bell, rung the bell, nobody came out. A worker happened to be walking by and so us sitting in the lobby and said, "Let me get someone for you." A woman comes to the front desk and says, "My apologies,  we are on lunch, but that's why we have this bell here." Told her I rang the bell,  she says they didn't hear it. Red flag #1. We go until a waiting room, the Dr. comes in and seems totally lost as to why we were there, although I sent the recommendation from MedVet, it was obvious she never read it. Red flag #2. She tells me they're going to give me a prescription for IBS, mind you we were there to get the GI panel to determine if my cat had IBS or not. Red flag #3. After explaining that, she actually read the doctor's notes and said yes, let's see what the blood panel shows. They ended up drawing the blood but she comes back asking to do something else due to some values being low when my cat left MedVet 3 weeks prior. I declined. Of course her levels were low she just had major surgery.  They then go and inspect two wounds my cat had. She comes back and says we have 2options, we can sedate and staple her wounds or we can just clip and clean them and give her an injection of antibiotic. I told her to clip and clean and give the antibiotic.  My cat slept the next 24 hours and ate nothing. I called around 11am the next day to ask if this was normal and was told yes, just wait around 2pm and she should be back to normal. Around 3pm I'm in full panic mode because my cat hasn't eaten since Wednesday night 10pm, and is STILL SLEEPING and lethargic. Was told again, she should be ok by dinner. I called again an hour later and was told, this is not normal, the antibiotic shouldn't have that effect, bring her in immediately.  There's no way I was taking my Cat back to that place. Luckily,  I forced some water down her throat and she threw up a yellowish substance, a lot. After that, she went and ate and started drinking again and was back to normal.  If you're serious about your animals health, this is NOT the place to take them.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience at this clinic.

I arrived approximately 15 minutes late to my appointment due to unexpected traffic. I explained the situation to the staff and emphasized that my pet was in significant pain and needed to be seen. Despite this, the clinic refused to examine my pet and insisted that I reschedule for two days later.

What made this especially frustrating was that there were still about 15 minutes remaining in my scheduled appointment slot, and there did not appear to be another patient immediately following us. I repeatedly asked if someone could at least take a quick look at my pet to determine whether the issue was urgent or if a follow-up visit would be needed. Instead, I was simply told to go to an emergency vet.

I understand that clinics have schedules and policies, but compassion and flexibility should also be part of veterinary care—especially when an animal is clearly in pain. A brief assessment could have made a significant difference and would have shown that the clinic prioritizes the well-being of its patients.

Unfortunately, this experience left me feeling that policy was valued more than the immediate needs of a suffering pet.

So today is here I arrived at approximately 5:18 waiting at the front desk as workers walked by then five minutes later a lady comes and calls my dogs name I say yes and she says your a little late we will have to charge a late fee your appointment was 5:15 for which I was told 5:30 and got no notification prior stating the exact time I just took the word of the lady behind the counter because they were on the phone with other for quite some time. So now I sit waiting to talk to the manager (KELLY) about why she want to charge me a $120+ for being early to the time I was given and 5 past Walmart they said it was. Today is 8/5/25

I had a 2:00 p.m. veterinary appointment scheduled for Saturday, June 21st at the Vetco clinic inside Petco at 4039 W. Diversey. I received multiple emails and text messages confirming the appointment, and I was even required to confirm twice or risk having it canceled.

When my car wouldn't start today, I tried calling to let them know—and that's when I discovered that the clinic is closed on Saturdays. So why was I allowed to schedule a Saturday appointment in the first place?

This isn't my first frustrating experience here. The vaccination clinic staff also previously messed up my senior dog’s heartworm medication, which was already a red flag. Between that and the fact that they clearly don’t have their scheduling systems under control, I’m done with this place.

If I hadn’t had car trouble, I would have driven all the way across town for absolutely nothing, AGAIN, since I had to make multiple trips out there last time to fix the issue with my dog's heartworm medication.

Completely unacceptable.

I hate leaving one star reviews, I'll start there.  We went for the first scheduled appointment visit and then waited over an hour to be seen.  After the incident with little accountability they offered to comp our fecal test.  It's now been 6 weeks and no one ever called us to confirm the results.  I was also promised that when I would receive that call that we could talk about getting the heartworm preventative.  The person I did speak with the day of the visit sent me home with my options and told me to review those so that when she called back I could tell her which one I preferred.

Now that I finally took it up on myself to call them, I left a message and no one called me back.  I then tried again today and reached someone.  She had little to say about my experience and could only tell me what the notes said, and said I would need to come back again for a heartworm test and that whatever I was told at the time was inaccurate.

She lacked any compassion for the mishaps, took no ownership as the customer facing support staff member, and couldn't tell me why no one ever called me back or offered any proactive solutions than just booking another appointment.

Somehow I fell through the cracks twice at Vetco which is disheartening as a customer.

This Vetco is the closest to me and brought both my cats in for a routine visit after moving back from California. The male vet had horrible bedside manner from the moment he walked into the exam room. He was judgmental as to how we take care of our cats. One of my cats has chronic allergies that affect her ears and he kept wanting to up-charge us for testing even though we had recent medical records on hand to prove her history with allergies (from another VETCO nonetheless). He was short with answers and would not prescribe her anything for her ear infection. Instead they shooed us away with a referral to another vet that did not even perform the services our cat needed. This made me uncomfortable and I was nervous for my cats to be taken to the back for their exam. I did some research and found the vetco in Elmhurst and they are amazing. Even though the drive is 45 minutes from the city it is absolutely worth taking your pets to that location. I left spending hundreds of dollars with not a single medication for the issues my cat was having. To say this person is a  “vet” is a joke. Beware and do your research, this place is a cash grab. If you’re looking for quality staff and service go to the location in Elmhurst.
